title: Opalite vs. GLOBO
summary: August 2026 comparison of Opalite Health vs. GLOBO KAI on clinical AI scope, language coverage, EHR integration, and documentation for hospitals.
body_markdown:
###


Choose Opalite Health if your priority is AI interpretation inside the exam room. GLOBO KAI is positioned for administrative and low-acuity touchpoints like scheduling and registration, while Opalite was built for real-time clinical conversations, including medication reconciliation, behavioral health, and discharge instructions, with an independent Johns Hopkins Medicine validation study behind it.


###


KAI supports 20-plus languages via AI; GLOBO's 430-plus figure is its human network. Opalite covers 150-plus languages and dialects, including 8 Spanish dialects, via AI directly, so thin-pool requests after hours do not automatically route to a human queue.


###


GLOBO is a strong fit for organizations that want AI layered onto a human interpreter network, primarily for front-desk and administrative workflows. Opalite is the better fit for hospitals and health systems that need AI to carry the full clinical encounter, generate multilingual documentation, integrate with Epic or other major EHRs, and cover a wide range of languages without scheduling an interpreter.


###


Yes. Opalite's AI scribe drafts structured notes, including SOAP and after-visit summaries, for provider review. GLOBO KAI does not generate clinical notes.


###


Opalite is HIPAA compliant, supports Business Associate Agreements, and maintains a SOC 2 Type II attestation. It also includes Opalite Guardian, an automated real-time quality framework designed to catch hallucinations, negation errors, and numeral errors before they reach the clinical record. GLOBO's Live Quality monitors human interpreter sessions but has not published an independent clinical validation study for KAI's AI accuracy in live medical encounters.
